nindian-polity-32-2.s: Under which clause does the Advocate General of a State hold office during the pleasure of the Governor?
nindian-polity-32-2.x: Article 165(3) says the Advocate General holds office during the Governor's pleasure; there is no fixed tenure.

nindian-polity-32-11.s: Which law officer has the right to speak in Parliament under Article 88?
nindian-polity-32-11.x: Article 88 rights belong to the Attorney General; the Solicitor General has no floor rights in Parliament.

nindian-polity-31-3.s: The remuneration of the Attorney General of India is determined by the:
nindian-polity-31-3.x: The President determines the Attorney General's remuneration, not Parliament.

n649f1e34b36.s: The office of the Solicitor General of India is governed by the:
n649f1e34b36.x: The Solicitor General is not mentioned in the Constitution; the post is statutory under the Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987.

n45786cc3e94.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 88 – Advocate General speaks in the State Legislature
Article 177 – Advocate General speaks in the State Legislature
Article 177 – Advocate General votes in the State Legislature
n45786cc3e94.x: Article 177 lets the Advocate General speak and take part in the State Legislature and its committees, but not vote; Article 88 is for the AG and Article 165 creates the Advocate General.

na0f0b43d55e.s: The Advocate General of a State must be qualified to be a judge of a:
na0f0b43d55e.x: The Advocate General must be qualified to be a High Court judge; the Attorney General must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge.

n530aefcf95e.s: The combined commission created by the 65th Amendment replaced the Special Officer and the commission set up by the Resolution of:
n530aefcf95e.x: The 65th Amendment (1990) commission replaced the original Special Officer for SCs and STs and the commission set up by the 1987 Resolution.

nindian-society-1-66.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First National Commission for Backward Classes – 1951
First constitutional recognition of OBC reservation – 1993
First State to introduce reservation – Kolhapur
First constitutional recognition of OBC reservation – 102nd Amendment
nindian-society-1-66.x: Kolhapur was the first State to introduce reservation; the 1st Amendment (1951) first recognised OBC reservation and the first NCBC came in 1993.

n14b9c006691.s: Which Constitutional Amendment restored the States' power to prepare their own lists of SEBCs?
n14b9c006691.x: The 105th Amendment, 2021 restored the States' power; the 102nd Amendment had let the President notify SEBCs.

n021d7f81ab9.s: The members of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes are appointed by the:
o: President by warrant under his hand and seal
n021d7f81ab9.x: The President appoints the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members by warrant under his hand and seal.

n32bf8d768b6.s: Besides the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson, the constitutional NCBC has how many members?
n32bf8d768b6.x: The constitutional NCBC has a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members; the earlier statutory NCBC had five members.

ndcb9c3afc95.s: While investigating a matter, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes has the powers of a:
ndcb9c3afc95.x: It has civil-court powers: summoning persons, requiring documents, receiving affidavits, requisitioning records and issuing commissions for witnesses.

n16235463ccb.s: The National Commission for Women is a statutory body under the:
n16235463ccb.x: The NCW is statutory under the NCW Act, 1990; there is no Article 338C. Article 338B is the NCBC.

n958c7529447.s: The Chairperson of which body was added as a deemed member of the NHRC by the 2019 amendment?
n958c7529447.x: The 2019 amendment added the NCBC and NCPCR chairpersons and the Chief Commissioner for PwD; the NCW, NCM and NCSC chairs were already deemed members.

na1b5161c915.s: The recommendations of the National Human Rights Commission are:
o: Not binding, though the government must respond
na1b5161c915.x: NHRC recommendations are not binding; the government must respond but the Commission cannot compel implementation.

n1c6255bd946.s: Which of the following powers does the National Commission for Women NOT have?
n1c6255bd946.x: The NCW can appoint committees, co-opt outsiders and regulate its own procedure, but cannot impose criminal sentences.

n990d8ba009a.s: The Chairperson, Members and Member-Secretary of the National Commission for Women are nominated by the:
n990d8ba009a.x: All of them are nominated by the Central Government, not appointed by the President.

n6144be92a9b.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NCM members – appointed by the President
NCM members – appointed by the Central Government
NCW members – appointed by the President
NCM members from minority communities – three
n6144be92a9b.x: NCM members are appointed by the Central Government; five of its seven members, including the Chairperson, are from minority communities.

n91cb11a77c7.s: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis functions under the Ministry of:
n91cb11a77c7.x: The NCSK is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, not the MWCD.

new.s: Which of the following is a limitation on the Attorney General of India?
o: He should not hold a brief against the Government of India
He is barred from private legal practice
He cannot appear in any High Court
new.x: The AG should not advise or hold a brief against GoI; he is not a full-time government servant, so he is not barred from private practice.

new.s: The Attorney General enjoys all the privileges and immunities of a Member of Parliament under:
new.x: Article 105(4) gives the AG the privileges of an MP; Article 194(4) does the same for the Advocate General in the State.

new.s: The Attorney General may defend an accused person in a criminal prosecution only with the permission of the:
new.x: The AG should not defend an accused in a criminal prosecution without the permission of the Government of India.

new.s: Who is the present Advocate General of Andhra Pradesh, reappointed on 19 June 2024?
new.x: Dammalapati Srinivas was reappointed Advocate General of AP on 19 June 2024; Subrahmanyam Sriram held the post earlier.

new.s: The Advocate General of Andhra Pradesh is appointed by the:
o: Chief Justice of the AP High Court
new.x: The Governor of AP appoints the Advocate General under Article 165.

new.s: In the order of precedence, the Attorney General of India is placed at number:
new.x: The AG is at No. 11; the Solicitor General is at 23 and the ASGs and Advocates General at 25.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Attorney General of India?
o: He is not a member of the Union Cabinet
His remuneration is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
He is part of the Union Executive
By custom he resigns when the Council of Ministers changes
new.x: The AG's remuneration is fixed by the President and is not charged on the Consolidated Fund.

new.s: A distinguished jurist can be appointed Attorney General if he is one in the opinion of the:
new.x: The AG must be qualified to be an SC judge, which includes being a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President.

new.s: The Attorney General and the Solicitor General are ex officio members of the Bar Council of India under the:
new.x: Under the Advocates Act, 1961 the AG and SG are ex officio members of the Bar Council of India.

new.s: The Solicitor General of India is regarded as the:
o: Chief legal adviser of the States
Head of the Union Law Ministry
new.x: The SG is the second law officer; he assists the AG, who is the first law officer.

new.s: The Attorney General represents the Government of India in Presidential reference cases under:
new.x: One duty of the AG is to represent GoI in Article 143 (Presidential reference) cases.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the duties of the Attorney General of India:
1. He appears for the Government of India in all Supreme Court cases concerning it.
2. He may be required to appear in any High Court.
3. He chairs joint sittings of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The AG appears for GoI in the Supreme Court and in any High Court when required; he does not chair joint sittings of Parliament.

new.s: Who was the Attorney General of India from 1998 to 2004?
new.x: Soli Sorabjee was AG 1998-2004; K.K. Venugopal was AG 2017-2022 and M.C. Setalvad was the first AG.

new.s: Who was the Attorney General of India from 2017 to 2022?
new.x: K.K. Venugopal was AG from 2017 to 2022, after Mukul Rohatgi; R. Venkataramani became AG on 1 October 2022.

new.s: The Advocate General enjoys the privileges of a member of the State Legislature under:
new.x: Article 194(4) gives the Advocate General the privileges of a State legislator; Article 105(4) is for the AG.

new.s: Instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for linguistic minority children is provided for in:
new.x: Article 350A directs States to provide mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage; Article 350B is the Special Officer.

new.s: The headquarters of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is at:
new.x: Its headquarters is New Delhi; it moved there from Allahabad in 2015.

new.s: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities submits reports to the:
new.x: The Special Officer reports to the President, who lays the reports before Parliament and sends them to the States.

new.s: Article 350B on the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was inserted by the:
new.x: Articles 350A and 350B were inserted by the 7th Amendment, 1956.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
new.x: The NCW is statutory (NCW Act, 1990); the NCST (338A), NCBC (338B) and Finance Commission (280) are constitutional.

new.s: NITI Aayog was set up by:
new.x: NITI Aayog is an executive body set up by a Cabinet resolution of 1 January 2015.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis:
1. It was originally a statutory body under a 1993 Act.
2. Its Act lapsed on 29 February 2004.
3. It is now a constitutional body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The NCSK Act of 1993 lapsed on 29 February 2004; since then the NCSK has been extended as a non-statutory body.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Commission for SCs and STs was created by a State Act of:
new.x: The AP State Commission for SCs and STs was created by a 2003 State Act.

new.s: The separate Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Tribes Act was passed in:
new.x: The AP State Commission for Scheduled Tribes Act is of 2020; the Assembly passed separate SC and ST Bills in December 2019.

new.s: The Second Backward Classes Commission headed by B.P. Mandal was appointed by the:
new.x: The Mandal Commission was appointed on 1 January 1979 by the Janata government of Morarji Desai.

new.s: Which Backward Classes Commission was the first to recommend 27% reservation for OBCs?
new.x: The Mandal Commission (1979) was the first to recommend 27% OBC reservation.

new.s: The term of the members of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes under the rules is:
new.x: Members serve a term of 3 years under the rules; tenure and service conditions are fixed by the President.

new.s: The civil-court powers of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes are provided in:
new.x: Article 338(8) gives the NCSC civil-court powers; Article 338(9) is about mandatory consultation.

new.s: Who is the present Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?
new.x: Kishor Makwana heads the NCSC (from March 2024); Suraj Bhan was its first chairperson.

new.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the combined National Commission for SCs and STs (1992)?
new.x: S.H. Ramdhan was the first chair of the combined commission; Suraj Bhan and Kunwar Singh were the first chairs of the separate NCSC and NCST.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Commissions for SCs and STs?
o: They can punish those who violate safeguards
State-related reports go to the Governor
Governments must consult them on major policy matters
new.x: The Commissions are not criminal courts and have no power to punish; their recommendations are advisory.

new.s: The separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was set up on:
new.x: The NCST under Article 338A was set up on 19 February 2004 after the 89th Amendment.

new.s: After the 2019 amendment, who can be appointed Chairperson of the NHRC?
o: Only a former Chief Justice of India
A former CJI or a former Judge of the Supreme Court
A former Chief Justice of a High Court
Any former Judge of a High Court
new.x: Since 2019 the NHRC chair can be a former CJI or a Supreme Court Judge; earlier only a former CJI.

new.s: After the 2019 amendment, the NHRC has how many human-rights members (at least one a woman)?
new.x: The 2019 amendment raised human-rights members from 2 to 3, at least one a woman.

new.s: The NHRC conforms to which international principles?
new.x: The NHRC conforms to the Paris Principles (Paris, Oct 1991; UNGA 20 Dec 1993).

new.s: After the 2019 amendment, human-rights work of which Union Territory stays with the NHRC?
new.x: The Centre may give UT human-rights work to SHRCs, but Delhi stays with the NHRC.

new.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in:
new.x: The UDHR was adopted on 10 December 1948; CEDAW is 1979, the Convention against Torture 1984 and the UNCRC 1989.

new.s: The total strength of the National Commission for Minorities, including the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson, is:
new.x: The NCM has a Chair, a Vice-Chair and 5 members, making 7.

new.s: The post of Vice-Chairperson was added to the National Commission for Minorities in:
new.x: The Vice-Chairperson post was added in 1995.

new.s: How many States have State Minorities Commissions?
new.x: There are 15 State Minorities Commissions, including Andhra Pradesh.

new.s: The National Commission for Minorities is a statutory body under the NCM Act of:
new.x: The NCM is statutory under the NCM Act, 1992 and was set up on 17 May 1993.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Commission for SCs and STs was reconstituted in:
new.x: The AP SC/ST Commission, created by a 2003 Act, was reconstituted in 2016.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Commission for Backward Classes was set up under an Act of:
new.x: The AP BC Commission is a permanent body under the AP Commission for BCs Act, 1993.

new.s: Who chairs the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes?
new.x: K.S. Jawahar chairs the AP SC Commission; Rayapati Sailaja chairs the AP State Commission for Women.

new.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission?
new.x: Justice Ranganath Misra was the first NHRC chair; Mohd. Sardar Ali Khan was the first NCM chair.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Commission – first Chairperson) is correctly matched?
new.x: Bhagwan Lal Sahni was the first NCBC chair; the first chairs of NCW, NHRC and NCM were Jayanti Patnaik, Ranganath Misra and Mohd. Sardar Ali Khan.

new.s: The National Human Rights Commission was set up on:
new.x: The NHRC was set up on 12 October 1993 under the PHRA, 1993, following an ordinance of 28 September 1993.

new.s: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis monitors the implementation of the:
new.x: The NCSK monitors the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013; the NCPCR monitors RTE, POCSO and JJ Acts.
